title: Out of the Whirlwind
backstory: Job and his friends argued back and forth for chapter after chapter, until the three of them finally ran out of answers (Job 32:1). What Job wanted was not advice but God himself — oh that I knew where I might find him, he said, that I might come even to his seat (Job 23:3). Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and his first words back were a question: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? (Job 38:1-4)

passages.synopsis: The LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind. He asked Job where he was when God laid the foundations of the earth, while the morning stars sang together. He asked who shut up the sea behind doors and told the proud waves how far they could come. Job had never faced questions so great.

God asked whether Job had ever commanded the morning or shown the dawn its place. He asked whether Job had walked in the springs of the sea or seen where light and darkness live. Job could not answer even one of these questions. Only the Maker of all things could.

God pointed Job to the night sky — the Pleiades, Orion, and the constellations in their seasons. He asked who leads them across the heavens, who counts the clouds, and who sends the rain on the earth. Even the lions and the young ravens look to God for their food. All creation depends on him.

God asked Job about the wild creatures he had made. The mighty horse paws in the valley and rushes toward battle without fear. The hawk flies by God's wisdom, and the eagle mounts up at his command to make her nest on high. She dwells upon the rock, on the crag of the rock, where no one else can climb. Every creature shows the power and care of its Maker.

scrambleVerses.text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?
Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?

hangmanWords.hint: God answered Job out of this
A cluster of stars God asked Job about
God clothed the horse's neck with this
She mounts up and nests on high

reflection: God answered Job with questions about stars, seas, and eagles. How does looking closely at God's creation change the way you see your troubles?
